name: Pashhur
overview: Pashhur was a male descendant of Immer and served as a chief officer in the Temple during the time of Jeremiah. His role as a temple official places him within the religious leadership of Israel, though his specific tribal affiliation is not recorded in Scripture. The details known about him come primarily from the book of Jeremiah.
namesAndTitles: The name Pashhur means '[perhaps] be quiet and round about,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name. Additionally, he was given the title Magor-missabib, meaning 'terror on every side,' a designation given by God that conveys a significant aspect of his character or role in the prophetic narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Pashhur as a descendant of Immer, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are recorded for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pashhur's importance lies in his position as a chief temple officer and his interaction with the prophet Jeremiah. The divine title Magor-missabib suggests that God used him to symbolize or enact a form of pervasive terror, indicating his role in the unfolding judgment and prophetic messages during a critical period in Israel's history.
